answer: Agents can make payments count only after a counterparty has locked funds for a fixed period and completed trades with several independently funded peers; a shared ledger checks that each peer’s stake predates the trade and was not recycled. This does not prove one person per identity, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: every fake account needs separate capital kept at risk, and splitting a stake cannot multiply its weight. A dune-colored interface, violet pigment, or fresh account names cannot bypass the ledger’s funding history.
